notes: Checked the four contested points and all hold. (1) `ὃν τρόπον` → *even as* as one `noncompositional` unit: neither the relative nor `τρόπον` answers to *as* or *even* separately (the corpus gloss of `ὅς` is *which*/*whom* and nothing renders *manner*), so rule 6 applies and rule 45's test agrees in principle; the accepted note already names the competing split reading per rule 16. Source head on the lexical noun (rule 10) and target head on *as* (rule 17) are both right. (2) The *even* belongs with the comparative, not with `οὕτως`: rule 82 records `καθώς` → *even as* as ordinary, and moving *even* to `οὕτως` would cross the alignment, which rule 100 forbids in the mirror case. So the bare *so* on s009 and *also* on s010 are correct under rules 100 and 65. (3) s017 `τὸν` `unrepresented` with *in mind* whole on `νοῦν`: the ASV writes no determiner for the noun, so rule 21's determinerless clause and rule 23 give the article nothing and keep the supplied case preposition on the noun. (4) `περὶ τὴν πίστιν`: `περί` is an expressed preposition with its own English word (rule 36), so the article takes a bare *the* under rule 19 and the noun stands alone — rule 21's *of the* pattern is not in question here.
